description.narrative: Montenegro's circular transition is hindered by limited industrial symbiosis frameworks, low private sector engagement, weak policy incentives, fragmented governance, and inadequate digitalization in waste tracking and resource efficiency, further exacerbated by economic reliance on linear consumption models, workforce skill gaps, and social exclusion, particularly among informal waste workers and women. 99.8% of enterprises in Montenegro are small and medium-sized (SMEs). They employ over 75% of the workforce and contribute around 70% of total value added2. Despite their key role in the Montenegrin economy, SMEs’ productivity is significantly lower than that of large counterparts coupled with higher vulnerability to shocks. The ILO participates in a joint UN initiative that aims to drive Montenegro’s transition to a circular economy by fostering industrial symbiosis, digital innovation, responsible business conduct (RBC), and capacity-building, ensuring both environmental sustainability and inclusive economic growth. ILO’s support contributes to a better understanding of the RBC environment under which Montenegrin small and medium-size enterprises operate and assists Montenegro in establishing policy frameworks conducive to promoting RBC. Subsequently, the ILO supports the development of tailored made training RBC programme to respond to existing needs including the sensitization and training of social partners and responsible government officials. Through these efforts, the ILO aims to strengthen economic resilience and greening while promoting RBC in sustainable enterprises.
